jurisdictions.name: Denver
notes: A zoning permit is required for all outdoor pools, barriers and fences. Building permits are not issued without sewer use and drainage (SUDP) approval, and single-family and duplex applications are submitted through ePermits.

The site plan must be drawn to scale and show the zoning setback lines, existing structures, pool dimensions, fences or barriers, how the pool meets the Energy Code (for example with a pool cover) and all related equipment.
A boundary survey is required if the pool or any equipment is within 3 feet of the property line.
Separate permits cover electrical work, plumbing for a pool heater or boiler, gas piping and recirculation piping, and mechanical work for indoor pool heaters.

sources.title: Permitting Guide for Residential & Commercial Pools, Spas, and Water Features (Denver Development Services)

jurisdictions.name: Lakewood
notes: A building permit is required for any pool, hot tub or spa on a residential property.
Lakewood says pools must meet its local amendments to the 2021 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, 2021 International Plumbing Code and 2021 International Residential Code.
The application and plans are uploaded through eTRAKiT; the plot plan must be at 1 inch = 30 feet or a larger scale.
Properties with a pool need a lockable cover or a fenced yard; the handout sets the fence at a minimum of 48 inches high.

sources.title: 2023 Residential Pool and Hot Tub Requirements - Lakewood

jurisdictions.name: Fort Collins
notes: The pool, pond or in-ground hot tub permit needs a building permit application, a scaled site plan and either manufacturer specifications or custom design details.
In-ground designs must include engineered foundation details, and plans must show safety barrier or cover details.
The page directs applicants to email the application to buildingservices@fortcollins.gov and does not name a portal for pool permits.

jurisdictions.name: Aurora
notes: Aurora lists the 2021 International Residential Code and the 2021 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code among its adopted codes.
The city's Building Division page says permits are applied for online.

sources.title: Adopted Building Codes - City of Aurora

jurisdictions.name: Colorado Springs (El Paso County)
notes: The Pikes Peak Regional Building Department's pool plan review handout says both onground portable (temporary) and permanent inground pools at a home require permits, but its Work Exempt From Permits page, citing Section 105.2 of the Pikes Peak Regional Building Code, lists above-ground swimming pools accessory to one- and two-family dwellings and R-3 occupancies that are less than 24 inches deep and not more than 5,000 gallons.

For a residential pool, the handout asks for a site plan showing the pool's location on the lot, dimensions to lot lines and adjacent structures, and all pool barrier requirements (the fence location or an automatic cover statement).

The same handout asks for a structural plan stamped by a Colorado licensed design professional, or an Evaluation Report from a nationally recognized testing laboratory for a prefabricated pool, and says onground portable pools do not need the structural plan.

The department says that, effective June 30, 2026, its code is the 2023 Pikes Peak Regional Building Code, 2nd Printing, which adopts by reference the 2021 ISPSC for swimming pools, the 2021 IRC for residential buildings and the 2023 NEC for electrical work.
